target.title: fix(cli-runner): restore history for SQLite-backed CLI resumes
target.body:
Related: #98236

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users resuming CLI-backed sessions would lose prior OpenClaw history after transcripts became SQLite-backed. Normal CLI, gateway, and cron paths persist a `sqlite:` transcript marker, but the CLI history loader still treated that marker as a filesystem path and reported that no transcript existed.

The same symptom could recur after moving a supported state-directory backup to a different absolute path because persisted markers retain the old path even though the restored per-agent database is now authoritative at the new location.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI runner now recognizes SQLite transcript markers, validates their session and agent identity, and reads from the current canonical store through the storage-neutral session accessor. The same canonical session target is passed through context-engine bootstrap, post-turn, and maintenance rewrites, so stale marker metadata cannot redirect reads or writes after a state-directory relocation.

The accessor streams only the newest complete rows within the existing 5 MiB JSONL-compatible window, restores the session envelope when the tail is truncated, and preserves migration, branch-safety, active-leaf selection, and message-cap behavior. Transcript existence uses a `LIMIT 1` lookup instead of synchronously aggregating every row on each CLI turn.

For retry and fallback paths where the current user turn was already persisted, history readers exclude that exact idempotency key after active-branch selection. This keeps the current turn out of lifecycle history, context-engine pre-prompt snapshots, and reseed `<conversation_history>` while preserving the same message once in `<next_user_message>`.

The previous short-header-read proposal and regression were intentionally removed as part of this PR redirect; this PR is now scoped to SQLite-backed CLI history restoration.

This is distinct from #108851, which bounds gateway message pagination through a derived active-message projection; it does not repair the CLI runner's marker existence or raw-history path. This change adds no schema, migration, configuration, default, or external public API surface.

## User Impact

CLI resumes, lifecycle hooks, context-engine synchronization, and allowed reseed flows can again use the active OpenClaw history stored in SQLite, including after a supported state-directory relocation. Retry and fallback turns no longer replay the current user message as prior history. Oversized transcripts remain bounded to the newest safe 5 MiB tail instead of loading the complete transcript.

## Evidence

- Initial RED on the test-first commit: [run](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29512957643), [job](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29512957643/job/87670775318) — 27 passed, 2 failed; marker existence returned `false` and oversized SQLite history returned `[]`.
- Review-gap RED: [run](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29520108279), [job](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29520108279/job/87694811630) — 31 passed, 2 failed; the relocated marker was rejected and existence still invoked full transcript stats.
- Memory-bound RED: [run](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29522181652), [job](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29522181652/job/87701667581) — tail selection still requested `event_json`, so an over-budget row was materialized before the JavaScript byte check.
- Context-target RED: [run](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29524447512), [job](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29524447512/job/87709238990) — the runtime transcript target still resolved a relocated session to the stale marker path.
- Live baseline RED through the real `pnpm openclaw agent --local` entry point with an isolated test-only CLI backend: [run](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29549165465), [job](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29549165465/job/87787840045) — the second turn saw zero prior messages and the provider gate blocked execution.
- Maintenance-target RED: [run](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29553169268), [job](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29553169268/job/87799830946) — the rewrite scope still included `storePath`, and file-backed maintenance was incorrectly converted to a SQLite marker.
- Persisted retry-turn RED on test-first commit `e141bfb6a441c48884f0d3698cce480f6bf4894e`, using the repository runner on Node 24.15.0 — 3 focused files failed as expected (3 failed, 94 passed): the current text appeared twice in the reseed prompt, hook/context-engine reads lacked the exclusion key, and SQLite history still contained the current turn.
- Final GREEN on exact fix head `d7a04d16f19baf2172ba45c654b2636497cf95a4`, pinned to base `44b01a1e5ab69357e46b0ec945b080290ef13873`: [run](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29557720712), [job](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29557720712/job/87813405498) — 10 focused files and 274 tests passed, including persisted retry-turn deduplication and a real two-database SQLite relocation rewrite control.
- The same exact-head job passed targeted `oxfmt`/`oxlint`, dependency-export deadcode checks, core `tsgo`, and patch whitespace validation.
- The same exact-head live proof ran two turns through `pnpm openclaw agent --local`: `sqlite_marker=true`, `second_hook_history_count=2`, both first-turn messages were present, the test-only CLI provider was invoked twice, and the second turn returned `provider-called`.
- Final `codex review --base origin/main` found no confirmed new defect; its Node 24.15.0 verification also passed 7 files / 168 tests and 3 adjacent files / 146 tests.

Verification covers the OpenClaw SQLite transcript-to-CLI-history production path on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu 24.04 with Node 24, isolated state/config/workspace data, and a test-only CLI backend. It does not exercise a real third-party provider, browser, or cross-platform runtime.
